report:
getaddrinfo EAI_AGAIN error

### Description

Using  a uptime kuma instance using docker on Ubuntu 22.04 aarch64 server in Oracle Cloud Platform  using the command
`docker run -d --dns=1.0.0.1 --restart=always -p 127.0.0.1:3001:3001 -v /opt/uptimekuma:/app/data  --name uptime-kuma louislam/uptime-kuma:1`

### 👟 Reproduction steps

1. docker run -d --dns=1.0.0.1 --restart=always -p 127.0.0.1:3001:3001 -v /opt/uptimekuma:/app/data  --name uptime-kuma louislam/uptime-kuma:1
2. Sign up
3. Add a new monitor 
4. Add SMTP notification service

### 👀 Expected behavior

The monitor should be up after the initial check

### 😓 Actual Behavior

The DNS resolution is failing which makes all the notification and uptime monitors to fails.

### 🐻 Uptime-Kuma Version

Version: 1.23.7 Frontend Version: 1.23.7

### 💻 Operating System and Arch

Ubuntu 22.04 LTS aarch64

### 🌐 Browser

Firefox

### 🐋 Docker Version

Docker version 24.0.7, build afdd53b

evidence.quote: I am able to ping google.com with your docker run command. It is likely a issue on your side.

confirmation.quote: After hours of debugging I found out that the problem is related to iptables. I reset the iptables like this - https://serverfault.com/a/633623 After restarting the docker service, it's working now!

notes: Container host networking (iptables) broken on a fresh Ubuntu host; no network even for ping/curl inside container, fixed by resetting iptables and restarting docker. Not an upgrade, not exotic topology.

reviews.decidable_why: The body shows the container cannot ping an IP or resolve any name, which is environmental and independent of the app.
Body shows total packet loss to an IP from inside the container, proving a host/container network problem independent of app code.
